text:
mira: Quick sync — after Friday's outage we need a concise playbook for graceful headroom degradation in dedicated GPU pools. Folklore and postmortem are messy, want something operators can run fast.

jamal: +1. Main failure mode was a sudden tail-latency spike in tenant A that starved prewarm credits and caused downstream eviction cascades.

li: We also saw weird fractional-MIG packing issues — pods couldn't fit and the shard kept spinning placements. That made scale-up slower.

mira: Proposal sketch: define a 3-stage degradation plan that is deterministic and reversible. Stage names: "soft-shed", "constrain", "overflow-route".

toni: short bullets please.

mira: TL;DR bullets: 1) soft-shed: reduce best-effort batch size + shrink in-memory prefix cache; 2) constrain: tighten admission for non-sla tenants and enable preemptible slots for anything below gold; 3) overflow-route: route a controlled fraction to shared-hosted variants or quantized model.

jamal: +1. Need exact trigger windows. Suggest triggers based on rolling p95 > threshold AND sustained token drop rate > X for 30s. Also hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.

li: Hysteresis key. Also add a small randomized delay before stage transitions to avoid thundering herd on fallback systems.

sanjay: Ops-runbook item: when in "constrain" stage, enable a readonly mode for heavy eval jobs and surface counts per-tenant in the console. We should also tag those requests for billing clarity.

kelsey: Can we embed tenant budget checks in the admission layer? If a tenant's reserved budget exhausted, auto-fall back.

mira: Yes — admission API needs a new enum for "degradation_tier" and a short token in the response so clients can report which fallback they hit.

alex: sample policy yaml (sketch):

```yaml
autoscale_policy_v2:
  degrade_on:
    tail_p95_ms: 1200
    sustained_token_loss_pct: 0.15
    window_secs: 30
  hysteresis_secs: 45
  stages:
    - id: soft_shed
      actions:
        - reduce_batch: 0.8
        - shrink_cache: 0.5
    - id: constrain
      actions:
        - admission: only_sla_high_and_gold
        - preemptible_enable: true
    - id: overflow_route
      actions:
        - route_fraction: 0.12
        - quantize_variant: 8bit_cached
```

jamal: Nice. Two operational notes: (A) route_fraction must be tenant-aware (don't ship all of tenant A at once), (B) quantify cost delta so finance knows.

mira: Good call. We'll add a per-tenant cap and expose expected cost delta in the rollout plan.

ops-bot: incident 2026-03-19-42 created by infra-bot — link: https://incidents.internal/2026-03-19-42 :rotating_light:

toni: During the incident, we also triggered a scale-down policy while degraded. Recommend a scale-down inhibit when any degradation stage active.

li: +1. Inhibit window should be longer than hysteresis, maybe 2x, to avoid oscillation.

sanjay: Manual override runbook: commands to force-stage and to drain/evict specifc tenant shards. Example: `/orbit force-degrade pool=eu-west-1 stage=constrain reason="tenant A spike"`

kelsey: Also add a reversible audit log entry for any manual overrides and who did them.

mira: Action items:
- jamal + li: draft concrete trigger thresholds and add MIG packing heuristics (owner: jamal)
- kelsey + sanjay: admission layer change to include degradation_tier and per-tenant caps (owner: kelsey)
- alex: add cost-estimate fields to policy and console surface (owner: alex)
- mira: write short RFC follow-up with playbook and runbook snippets, then schedule 30m sync.

jamal: I'll start a PR for policy schema and unit tests.

li: I'll add a small simulator to reproduce fractional MIG packing failure in CI.

mira: Thanks — please @me when PRs land. I'll put the RFC draft in docs/rfcs and link from console playbook. :eyes:
